# tests Module Context

## When To Read This

Read this before changing test harness behavior, shared fixtures, Playwright/e2e setup, Bun preload/isolation, broker-backed integration coverage, Control API schema validation, visual/accessibility assertions, task/relay regression tests, or CI-facing test commands. Production modules remain semantic authority; tests document executable contracts and failure modes.

## Ownership And Boundaries

`tests` owns unit, integration, snapshot, Playwright/e2e, schema, fixture, and real-broker regression contracts under `tests/**`. It does not own production behavior, generated schemas, browser bundles, screenshots, or broker binaries. When tests appear to define behavior, route to the corresponding production module first, then use tests for expected observable outcomes and regression intent.

`bunfig.toml` now preloads `tests/test-preload.ts` for Bun tests; although the config file is contextless, test isolation semantics belong here. The preload creates an owned temporary `WOLFPACK_TASK_RELAY_ROOT` and removes it after the test run, preventing local relay state leakage.

## Test Families

- **Unit tests (`tests/unit/**`):** parser/contract helpers, route wiring, provider detection, setup/service/build/install policies, terminal hydration/loading/resize logic, task/relay stores, quiet-alert policy, session activity, browser UI helpers, and regression tests for bug-prone boundaries.
- **Integration tests (`tests/integration/**`):** HTTP route behavior, auth/rate/CSP, Control API schema contract, machine/Tailnet contracts, task gateway/relay behavior, broker backend/client boundaries, and PTY/WS dispatch flows that do not require a full browser.
- **E2E tests (`tests/e2e/**`):** Playwright browser flows across desktop/mobile profiles, optional real broker usage, session/grid/delegation/Tailnet interactions, passive inspection, task-worker readiness, visual makeover, and accessibility/navigation behavior.
- **Snapshot tests (`tests/snapshot/**`):** service descriptor/plist/systemd shape.
- **Broker Rust tests (`broker/tests/**`):** live in the broker module but are coupled to this test strategy for real socket/FFI validation.

## High-Value Contracts

### Test environment isolation

- `tests/test-preload.ts` owns task-relay temp-root isolation for Bun tests. New tests that depend on durable relay state should not use the operator's default `~/.wolfpack` path.
- `tests/e2e/test-server-home.ts` creates/removes only owned temporary homes with a marker token, verifies canonical temp parent, rejects symlink/non-owned paths, and refuses broad deletion. Use it for e2e server-home cleanup instead of ad hoc `rm -rf` paths.
- `WOLFPACK_TEST` enables test-only hooks and shorter cache TTLs in production modules. Tests may use those hooks; production code must not depend on them.

### Schema and docs publication tests

`tests/control-api-schema-validator.ts`, `tests/unit/control-api-schema*.test.ts`, and `tests/integration/control-api-schema-contract.test.ts` compare runtime contracts against `src/control-api/schema.ts` and `docs/generated/control-api.schema.json`. Stable API changes must update schema source and regenerate docs; do not hand-edit generated artifacts to satisfy tests.

### Task-worker readiness coverage

- `tests/unit/task-worker-readiness.test.ts` covers launch-resource preflight, executable symlinks vs dangling/missing resources, exact session/project/harness/liveness checks, deadline handling, endpoint lookup, and exact-ID cleanup outcomes.
- `tests/e2e/task-worker-readiness.e2e.ts` optionally launches real Pi + Pi Tasks against an isolated broker/relay when prerequisites exist. Skips are environmental; a pass proves exact live session ID, Pi harness, project root, relay endpoint, and exact-ID teardown.
- `tests/e2e/task-worker-early-exit.e2e.ts` covers readiness failure when the worker exits too early.

### Passive inspection and terminal conflict coverage

`tests/e2e/broker-passive-inspection.e2e.ts` verifies that Inspect on an occupied-session overlay uses a bounded exact-ID snapshot, opens no extra `/ws/pty`, leaves the original controller in control, preserves broker geometry, refreshes stale/non-live text, and can inspect recently exited tombstoned sessions where supported. Related unit tests cover `session-inspector`, `session-snapshot`, terminal loading UI, and broker/backend exact-ID snapshot contracts.

### Activity, idle filter, and quiet alerts

- `tests/unit/session-activity-observation.test.ts`, `tests/unit/quiet-alert-policy.test.ts`, `tests/unit/push.test.ts`, and `tests/unit/agent-runtime-state-batching.test.ts` cover rendered-output fingerprints, policy epochs, delivery ownership, debounce/retry, recipient generation freezing, and batched runtime-state persistence.
- `tests/e2e/idle-session-view.e2e.ts` and updated session-state visualization tests exercise the All/Idle filter and dashboard activity states from user-visible flows. Idle status should come from typed runtime state, not terminal prose assertions.

### Browser UI, grid, visual, and accessibility coverage

- `tests/e2e/visual-makeover.e2e.ts`, `ui-polish`, `ux-navigation`, `accessibility-navigation`, and `axe-accessibility` suites assert the current design contract: original wolf identity, case-preserving session typography, compact All/Idle segmented control, bounded dialogs, visible destructive controls, mobile targets, and reduced motion.
- Grid tests assert distinct grid/session actions, conflict overlays, take-control fallback, keyboard reordering, and per-cell terminal isolation expectations. When UI markup changes, update data-action delegation and accessibility assertions together.
- `tests/unit/session-card-view.test.ts`, `terminal-bootstrap.test.ts`, `terminal-loading-ui.test.ts`, and related public-helper tests are the fastest checks for small browser-helper changes.

### Broker-backed tests

- E2E/integration helpers under `tests/e2e/broker-helpers.ts` and `tests/e2e/test-server-broker.ts` start real broker/server stacks when available. Respect `skipIfNoBroker`; skipped broker tests are not proof of broker behavior.
- Broker passive inspection, reconnect, takeover, scrollback, lifecycle, mobile copy, and shell/TUI tests are cross-module blast-radius checks for any broker protocol, server WS, or browser hydration changes.

## Cross-Module Coupling Notes

- Session create/open/task-worker tests couple `src/cli/session-control.ts`, API routes, session contracts, `BrokerBackend`, task-relay gateway/store, docs/session-control, and the Pi skill.
- Passive inspection tests couple broker snapshots/tombstones, `BrokerBackend.captureSessionSnapshotById`, `SessionSnapshotService`, browser conflict overlays, `session-inspector`, Control API schema/docs, and real-broker e2e fixtures.
- Quiet-alert/activity tests couple session observation, push delivery, settings persistence, browser session cards, generated schema, and notification e2e flows.
- Visual/accessibility tests couple `public/index.html`, `public/styles.css`, app/grid/session-order markup, screenshots/docs assets, and site assets, but screenshots remain evidence only.
- Provider/setup/service tests couple CLI setup, provider readiness, initial settings, service descriptor snapshots, install scripts, package metadata, and docs.

## Read/Change Gotchas

- Prefer narrow unit/integration tests for logic and reserve Playwright for browser/runtime behavior; broad visual/e2e runs can be slow and environment-sensitive.
- Do not use terminal text scraping in tests when structured session/task status exists. Stable `sessionId` is the expected automation handle.
- When tests use real Pi, real broker, Tailscale, or browser profiles, skips must be explicit and environmental. Do not convert missing capability into a passing assertion.
- Fake timers are used for timing-sensitive cleanup/retry logic where possible; avoid wall-clock sleeps in unit tests unless validating real browser/broker behavior.
- Keep generated schema/site/screenshots synchronized through the production generation pipeline; tests should catch drift, not bless hand edits.
